Scheme.name: Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai
Scheme.description: Monthly basic income assistance to eligible women heads of households. In December 2025 the programme was expanded by about 13–17 lakh women, taking coverage to roughly 1.31 crore beneficiaries; the 2026-27 allocation was reported at ₹13,807 crore. The new government announced (May 2026) an intent to raise the assistance to ₹1,500 in phases — not yet implemented as of this verification.
Scheme.eligibility: Eligible women heads of family meeting income and other criteria as notified.
Scheme.benefits: ₹1,000 per month paid directly to bank accounts (proposed increase to ₹1,500 pending official orders).
Scheme.beneficiaries: About 1.31 crore women (Dec 2025 expansion; figures as reported by official statements and The Hindu/dtnext).
Scheme.applicationProcess: As per the department’s notified procedure — follow the official source link.
Scheme.documentsRequired: Per scheme guidelines — confirm on the official application portal.
Scheme.verificationNote: Beneficiaries aged 60+ are being migrated to the Old Age Pension scheme (May 2026 announcements) to raise their monthly assistance.

Scheme.name: Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme
Scheme.description: Free nutritious breakfast on school working days for government-school students. Retained and renamed under the new government: on 22 Sep 2026 CM C. Joseph Vijay launched its expansion to Classes VI–VIII (earlier Classes I–V), adding about 15.30 lakh students.
Scheme.eligibility: Students of Classes I–VIII in government schools.
Scheme.benefits: Hot cooked breakfast each working day.
Scheme.beneficiaries: About 15.30 lakh additional students from the September 2026 expansion (official launch coverage).
Scheme.applicationProcess: As per the department’s notified procedure — follow the official source link.
Scheme.documentsRequired: Per scheme guidelines — confirm on the official application portal.
Scheme.sourceName: Government of Tamil Nadu — launch coverage (The Hindu, Deccan Herald: 22 Sep 2026)
Scheme.verificationNote: Renamed from "Chief Minister’s Breakfast Scheme"; expansion announced at the 22 Sep 2026 official launch.

Scheme.benefits: Home visits by health workers, free medicines and follow-up.
Scheme.beneficiaries: Over 1 crore beneficiaries (launch-era figure, pending re-verification).

Announcement.title: Government appeals for an eco-friendly Deepavali 2026
Announcement.body: Press Release No.984 (3 Nov 2026): the Government of Tamil Nadu appeals to the public to celebrate Deepavali 2026 with minimal noise and air pollution, in line with Supreme Court timings on firecracker use.

Announcement.title: ₹3,000 crore credit disbursed to women self-help group members
Announcement.body: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay disbursed ₹3,000 crore in credit support to women SHG members (about 26,000 members reported) to expand livelihood enterprises — an early flagship welfare push of the new government.
Announcement.sourceName: Government of Tamil Nadu (reported by India Today & Daily Pioneer, Nov 2026)

Announcement.title: 26 special POCSO courts and 4 NDPS courts ordered
Announcement.body: The Government of Tamil Nadu has ordered the establishment of 26 special courts to try cases under the POCSO Act and four special courts for NDPS cases, strengthening fast-track justice (press release, 1 Nov 2026).

Announcement.title: Tamil Nadu Semiconductor Ecosystem Scheme 2026 launched
Announcement.body: CM C. Joseph Vijay launched the Semiconductor Ecosystem Scheme 2026 to boost investment and position Tamil Nadu as a premier semiconductor hub, with support for fabs, design firms and a skilled workforce pipeline.
Announcement.sourceName: Government of Tamil Nadu (The Hindu, 16 Oct 2026)

Announcement.title: Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar takes full-time charge as Governor of Tamil Nadu
Announcement.body: Following the October 2026 gubernatorial appointments by President Droupadi Murmu, Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar — who had held additional charge since 12 March 2026 while Governor of Kerala — became full-time Governor of Tamil Nadu.
Announcement.sourceName: Lok Bhavan, Tamil Nadu / The New Indian Express (13 Oct 2026)

Announcement.title: By-election results: TVK wins Madurantakam and Dharapuram
Announcement.body: Counting for the two assembly by-elections held for seats vacated by AIADMK MLAs who joined TVK concluded on 9 Oct 2026: TVK’s K. Maragatham Kumaravel won Madurantakam (74,048 votes) and P. Sathyabama won Dharapuram (66,841 votes, margin 9,471). Five assembly seats remain vacant.
Announcement.sourceName: Election Commission of India — by-election results (9 Oct 2026)

Announcement.title: Expanded Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme launched
Announcement.body: CM C. Joseph Vijay launched the expansion of the breakfast scheme to students of Classes VI–VIII at an official function on 22 Sep 2026, adding about 15.30 lakh students to the programme.
Announcement.sourceName: Government of Tamil Nadu (The Hindu & Deccan Herald, 22 Sep 2026)

Announcement.title: Budget 2026-27 presented — maiden budget of the 17th Assembly government
Announcement.body: Finance Minister Dr. N. Marie Wilson presented the state budget for 2026-27 on 5 Aug 2026: total expenditure ₹4,72,585 crore, capital outlay ₹56,985 crore, ₹44,527 crore for school education, ₹812 crore for the new Annan Seer Thittam (8-gram gold coin and silk saree for eligible brides), gold rings for newborns and free laptops announced. A white paper on the state’s financial position was also announced.
Announcement.sourceName: Finance Department — Budget Speech 2026-27 (PRS Legislative Research analysis)

Announcement.title: Government formation: C. Joseph Vijay sworn in as 22nd Chief Minister
Announcement.body: After TVK won 108 of 234 seats in the April 2026 election (counting 4 May), C. Joseph Vijay was sworn in as Chief Minister on 10 May 2026. The council of ministers was expanded to 35 members on 21–22 May 2026, with portfolios allocated with the Governor’s approval.
Announcement.sourceName: Government of Tamil Nadu — Council of Ministers

Announcement.title: 2026 Legislative Assembly election held across 234 constituencies
Announcement.body: Elections to the 17th Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly were held on 23 April 2026 with counting on 4 May 2026: TVK 108 seats (35.07% votes), DMK 59 (24.28%), AIADMK 47 (21.30%), with the balance to allies and others. Full constituency-wise results are on the ECI portal.
Announcement.sourceName: Election Commission of India — 2026 TN general election results

CalendarEvent.title: First Session of the 17th Legislative Assembly
CalendarEvent.description: The first session of the newly constituted 17th Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly sat from 11 May to 8 Sep 2026 (28 sitting days; 13 Bills passed, 9 government resolutions and 17 Rule 110 announcements).
CalendarEvent.sourceNote: Session record as per the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly (tnla.neva.gov.in) and assembly reporting.

CalendarEvent.description: The assembly’s session calendar lists a session in November 2026. Exact dates to be confirmed from the official session calendar.
CalendarEvent.sourceNote: Session calendar at tnla.neva.gov.in lists a November 2026 session; exact sitting dates pending confirmation. Placeholder date shown until verified.

CalendarEvent.title: By-elections to vacant assembly constituencies
CalendarEvent.description: By-elections to the remaining vacant seats (Tiruchirappalli East, Perundurai, Ambasamudram, Viralimalai, Karur) per ECI notifications. Madurantakam and Dharapuram were filled on 9 Oct 2026.
CalendarEvent.sourceNote: Polling dates for the five vacant ACs pending the latest ECI notification (earlier process reported to be affected by litigation). Placeholder date shown until verified.

Complaint.title: Sewage overflow near corporation school
Complaint.description: Untreated sewage is overflowing on the street adjoining the corporation school for three weeks. Children walk through stagnant water to reach the school gate. Request urgent desilting of the blocked line and disinfection.

Complaint.title: Street lights not working for a month
Complaint.description: Nine of eleven streetlights in the lane are non-functional after the last spell of rain. Two-wheelers skid at night; residents request immediate replacement of fittings.
Complaint.resolutionNote: All fittings replaced with LED luminaires and wiring repaired. Verified during night inspection on 28 Oct.

Complaint.title: Drinking water tanker not reaching street 4
Complaint.description: Tanker schedule shows daily supply but tankers have not entered street 4 for eleven days. Residents including elderly persons are buying water.

Complaint.title: Potholes on school road causing accidents
Complaint.description: Two-wheelers are skidding on the pothole-ridden stretch near the government school. Two minor falls reported this month. Request cold-mix patchwork immediately and re-tarring after monsoon.

Complaint.description: An intermediary at the local body office demanded ₹15,000 to expedite building plan approval and hinted approval will otherwise be delayed. Requesting confidential enquiry and action.

Complaint.description: The primary health centre in our block functions without a medical officer on Tuesdays for the past month, affecting the weekly maternal check-up camp.
Complaint.resolutionNote: Medical officer posting regularised and a standby roster notified. Camp schedule restored.

Complaint.title: Anganwadi building roof leak
Complaint.description: Roof of the anganwadi building leaks during rain; children’s activities shifted to the community hall. Request roof repair with waterproofing.

Complaint.title: Mid-day meal quality complaint
Complaint.description: Eggs supplied under the nutrition menu have been stale on two days this week. Request inspection and quality check of supplier consignments.

Complaint.title: Encroachment blocking stormwater drain
Complaint.description: Shops have extended ramps over the stormwater drain causing waterlogging in the lane during rains. Request enforcement and restoration of drain section.
Complaint.resolutionNote: Reopening of drain verified as completed under an earlier works order; lane-level waterlogging traced to private plot grading outside corporation scope. Advised applicant of the correct forum.

Complaint.title: Bus shelter damaged and unsafe
Complaint.description: The bus shelter on the route collapsed partially in the last storm; the roof sheet hangs loose over waiting passengers.
Complaint.resolutionNote: Shelter dismantled and rebuilt with new roofing; safety inspection completed.
